<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mhc-cde7f1ea" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4bdf0d3f962113ce">What freedom do multiple residual streams add?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They exchange information dynamically, build attention/FFN inputs, and write back to several streams. Mixing needs constraints because it can amplify depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep different histories and mix as needed rather than using one cumulative vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4bdf0d3f962113ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5c14b4fa80176f3">Why constrain mHC residual mixing to a doubly stochastic matrix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated unconstrained mixing can amplify deep residual signals. Nonnegative entries and unit row/column sums constrain exchanges while retaining communication. This does not bound growth of the whole nonlinear network.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two streams can mix 0.7/0.3 under both constraints; repeated unconstrained sums may grow quickly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5c14b4fa80176f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec35693c6afdc398">Why is mHC more than another normalization layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It restricts residual maps to nonnegative doubly stochastic matrices and pre/post maps to nonnegative values. Hidden normalization does not impose those operator constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalized outputs do not imply row and column sums of one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec35693c6afdc398">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-38438b55be6098ad">Are unit row sums enough to validate mHC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Check nonnegativity and unit column sums as well as separate pre/post constraints. A nonexpansive residual mixer does not prove the full nonlinear model is nonexpansive or better trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two rows concentrating on one column satisfy row sums but fail column sums.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38438b55be6098ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mild-b3546e10" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bdca93044e6a6ea">Why can imbalance hurt rare specialist experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broad experts can dominate router learning despite specialists serving particular inputs. Expert-specific margins and full training reward structure retain more information than hard minimum-cost labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Majority-oriented training may ignore a specialist for a rare question type.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bdca93044e6a6ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-389a19e2fa152f10">Why vary expert margins rather than add minority class weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Margins change score separation geometry; weights scale loss contributions. mild retains full training costs or rewards instead of reducing each to a winner. Estimate margins on training and never read unknown expert costs at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hard minimum-cost labels can discard near-ties involving a specialist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-389a19e2fa152f10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78a4ff69f6b86315">What does full expert cost/reward supervision retain over argmin labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Argmin keeps only the winner. A cost-based surrogate and expert margins preserve differences and relative score constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A close second and an expensive second need not give identical supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78a4ff69f6b86315">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f693c043591f964e">May mild route using true candidate costs at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Routing uses inference features only; costs and labels are unavailable. Fit margins on train and select on validation. Use stable log-sum-exp and choose the highest expert index on ties as specified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training knows answer costs; a new question does not reveal who answers correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f693c043591f964e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mirror-moe" data-paper-title="Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mirror-moe-43695dbb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd36506392655d60">Why select near-boundary experts early?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amirror-moe">Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant shared experts and many fine-grained combinations can obscure alternatives. Mirror routing temporarily suppresses some usual winners to train other combinations, then anneals back.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Avoid always giving the same winners every early token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22353">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22353-mirror-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd36506392655d60">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mirror-moe" data-paper-title="Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2750f3a34fee37eb">Should MirrorMoE use mixed mirror probabilities to weight outputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amirror-moe">Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mix forward and negated-logit distributions for exploratory selection only, annealing back to standard routing. Selected outputs retain original probabilities. Track actual dispatch separately; mixing or renormalizing output weights changes the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A low-probability expert can run for exposure without receiving a larger output coefficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22353">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22353-mirror-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2750f3a34fee37eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mirror-moe" data-paper-title="Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccb0ea3c337d2306">How does mirror selection differ from arbitrary router noise?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amirror-moe">Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Apply softmax to negated logits and mix with original probabilities using an annealing coefficient. Arbitrary noise does not reproduce its distribution or endpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At ρ=0, selection returns to ordinary top-k.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22353">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22353-mirror-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccb0ea3c337d2306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mirror-moe" data-paper-title="Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dde9c8ec3f02b8fe">Which probabilities and frequencies enter MirrorMoE&#x27;s load term?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amirror-moe">Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use actual dispatch frequencies and original ξ, not mixed p. Aggregate outputs with original weights and Z=1 without renormalizing selected experts. Selection, load, and aggregation differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mirror probability can change whether an expert runs, but not its original output weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22353">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22353-mirror-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dde9c8ec3f02b8fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-msar-f6753b95" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bde517456b599ffc">Why retrieve earlier depth representations at the current layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary residuals accumulate updates in one vector. MSAR makes full-width views at several time scales and retrieves across depth to access history differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use raw, short-window, and smoother views to form a layer input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bde517456b599ffc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9afa7d02b04dbe76">How do MSAR streams differ from channel-split heads, and where does softmax apply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each stream keeps the full hidden vector at a different sequence scale. Softmax retrieves depth sources separately per stream; sigmoid combines retrieved streams without unit-sum weights. Persistent expanded views also change cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raw, short, and long views each contain full vectors, then independently choose historical layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9afa7d02b04dbe76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef3b4f6b4d48eb99">How does Block MSAR&#x27;s persistent summary differ from caching all expanded views?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Store embeddings, completed block summaries, and the current partial sum only. Expand streams at read time; permanently storing them changes capacity and lifetime.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four views can serve one read without retaining four historical copies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef3b4f6b4d48eb99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-909ebec9f386a484">Is a zero source harmless before a block has a partial sum?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Zero still enters the depth softmax denominator and dilutes other sources. Omit the absent partial, and use sigmoid rather than stream softmax in the final mixer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A zero vector added to two valid sources changes their normalized weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-909ebec9f386a484">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:novelty-patching" data-paper-title="Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-novelty-patching-3454dd1e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5a318b9dcdf5183">Why use recent repetition to choose byte patches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anovelty-patching">Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher, Chile</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Byte patches reduce global calls. Recent match length captures repeatability, and a cheap two-byte predictor estimates novelty instead of relying only on entropy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A recently seen span may be reusable, whereas a novel span may need finer boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22100">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22100-novelty-patching/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5a318b9dcdf5183">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:novelty-patching" data-paper-title="Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b724f96d1642e069">Why use matching length offline but a two-byte lookup online?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anovelty-patching">Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher, Chile</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Longer recent matches define offline novelty labels. Deployment uses a prefix-indexed table and low-count fallback instead of reading a future span. Offline labels are not available when deciding a boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with full template matches, then estimate from the two already generated bytes online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22100">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22100-novelty-patching/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b724f96d1642e069">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:novelty-patching" data-paper-title="Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-320494967794fa3e">How does a two-byte table differ from recomputing future match length online?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anovelty-patching">Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher, Chile</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future match lengths are offline labels. Deployment uses already generated bytes and a frozen threshold; looking past the current position leaks future information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not inspect whether the next 16 unseen bytes occurred before generating them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22100">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22100-novelty-patching/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-320494967794fa3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:novelty-patching" data-paper-title="Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1021385673b04f4">How does Novelty Patching handle rare byte pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anovelty-patching">Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher, Chile</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Below 20 observations, back off to one-byte means, then the global mean. Calibrate τ on training bytes and reset history at document boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One observed match should not determine online boundaries for a rare pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22100">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22100-novelty-patching/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1021385673b04f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-penelope-d7b5f7a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b87f8634f7737374">What does Penelope repeatedly refine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A continuous hidden state at a local decoder boundary, with shared latent blocks and a gate before higher layers. It does not emit visible text on every loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refine one hidden position twice instead of writing the answer twice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b87f8634f7737374">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b2c14cdd216b4ff">Why not rerun the full decoder for Penelope latent steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared recurrent transform and gated state refine one decoder boundary repeatedly. Only that local computation increases; task gains require measurement and loop count is not reasoning ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refine a structured problem three times at the boundary without rerunning completed lower layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b2c14cdd216b4ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fa1f888e57520c1">How does local recurrence differ from repeating the whole decoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It only repeats the designated latent block. Full reruns repeat lower and upper layers as well. Equal step counts do not match compute or information paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two small block calls cost less than two complete passes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fa1f888e57520c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b562a434d9d3e865">Can K independent layers replace K Penelope updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Recurrence reuses Fθ and GRU/time gates; independent layers add parameters and alter the constraint. The local budget omits the paper&#x27;s CoT-to-latent curriculum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reusing one block twice differs from running two separately parameterized blocks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b562a434d9d3e865">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-persistent-recurrent-memory-f4545966" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3978cf78534be1dc">What extra state does Persistent Recurrent Memory add?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Between layer groups, current representations observe and update a persistent recurrent state that then influences computation through gates. It is distinct from residual accumulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Earlier extracted information can persist and assist the subsequent layer group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3978cf78534be1dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0437ea764b0b567">What path changes when persistent recurrent memory sits between decoder halves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observe the intermediate state, update persistent state with a GRU, then gate its influence into later layers. This is neither a static prefix nor unconditional addition. Capacity and reset boundaries remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One layer group observes a new constraint and the next can use the updated memory if relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0437ea764b0b567">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-590da0611d2065db">How does persistent GRU memory differ from a residual connection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A residual passes representation through the current graph. Observe–update–influence maintains extra state with a separate lifetime and update rule. It is not infinite token storage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A persistent state can survive without reconstructing prior inputs word for word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-590da0611d2065db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ab1a8e897c2a7e5">Can observe, GRU update, and gated influence be reordered?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not without changing the topology. Specify observation source, old state, and whether later layers read pre- or post-update state; compare a reference. Local checks do not reproduce full TinyStories curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading old state before updating differs from influencing with freshly updated state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ab1a8e897c2a7e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rare-2c269dff" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc4d553de67c183b">Why can direct activation steering change expert selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The router reads hidden state. Editing it can move expert logits and alter the computation path, confounding behavioral effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An intended style change may also send the token to different experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc4d553de67c183b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cea8b60a2a7e1dd">How does RARE steer representations without rerouting MoE tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct edits can change router-visible coordinates. Project edits into the current router&#x27;s nullspace, then remove newly visible drift at protected later layers. This separates behavior edits from route changes, not all nonlinear effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remove a style edit&#x27;s routing component initially and correct drift after intervening transformations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cea8b60a2a7e1dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-39d4464837c8641a">How does RARE nullspace projection differ from reducing edit strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A smaller edit can still shift logits. Nullspace projection gives RΔh=0 for the protected linear router. Behavioral improvement still needs measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny nonzero score change can cross top-k; the nullspace removes that direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39d4464837c8641a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cec1da896a037b6">Why correct later protected layers after the first projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonlinear propagation can create new router-visible components. At each protected layer, project the edited-minus-clean difference into that router&#x27;s nullspace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first router can stay unchanged while the next one needs correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cec1da896a037b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rd-attnres-0af1c94e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2dbf02acbee4394">Does depth routing choose tokens or historical layer representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It combines residual sources from different depths, separately for QK and V, not token-level experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use deeper matching features for QK and shallower content for V.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2dbf02acbee4394">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c920aab21c83511">Why add a separate depth route for V but retain shared Q/K routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Q/K determine matching while V supplies retrieved content. RD-AttnRes retains the source set and attention mechanism, but learns separate depth weights for content. Routing does not create new source information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Q/K can favor deep semantics while V preserves shallow lexical details.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c920aab21c83511">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-522bf38df751fe6c">What does the Block AttnRes comparison hold fixed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residual sources and main attention stay the same; only V gets an independent depth route. This isolates role separation rather than changing the backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both arms read the same layer set, with one allowing different V weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-522bf38df751fe6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-df03297540c04364">Should Q and K also get separate routes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Both use h_QK, with h_V separate. Splitting Q/K adds another variable. Check actual weight divergence without treating it as guaranteed PPL improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Q and K project from one mixed representation, while V projects from another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df03297540c04364">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-repeat-aware-moe-d00603e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c3245386450ca45">Why treat repetition as an independent variable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same tokens can contain different unique information. Repetition can worsen expert memorization; study its interaction with sparsity and regularizers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten reads of 10,000 examples differ from one read of 100,000 examples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c3245386450ca45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ca7b821059ada2f">Why can repeated data affect MoE and dense models differently at equal token counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token count does not equal unique information. Routed experts may memorize repeated samples faster. Study stronger masking/dropout, and use held-out data; decreasing train loss is insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten passes over one corpus differ from ten distinct corpora despite equal token budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ca7b821059ada2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ddb2721518f32a1">Is matching steps enough to compare repeated-data overfitting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match or report total tokens, unique data, repetition, and sparsity. The work studies memorization under these conditions, not universal MoE inferiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one arm sees more repeats, architecture alone cannot explain its generalization gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ddb2721518f32a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-afab03669f00de24">How should a local repeat-aware schedule be accepted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check that repeat and sparsity actually change masking/dropout according to the definition, and record applied settings. State-transition fixtures are not large pretraining or generalization evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Higher repetition should alter effective regularization, not just a config name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-afab03669f00de24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sparse-decoding-1beb4b13" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-67d3d31ea69b4ff3">Why separate activation collection from the pruning algorithm?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The protocol collects actual autoregressive decode activations and passes them to a backend. Substituting Wanda does not implement SparseGPT&#x27;s optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different pruners can consume the same decode activations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67d3d31ea69b4ff3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f80ad83e68dcf05f">Why calibrate SparseDecoding on actual decode activations and exclude prefill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deployment generates its own prefixes, whose states differ from teacher-forced and prefill states. Collect genuine dense autoregressive activations before pruning. Collection protocol is separate from SparseGPT or Wanda backend choices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A self-generated departure from the reference can use channels that teacher-forcing calibration never sees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f80ad83e68dcf05f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0aab02eef15816d">Does local Wanda use the same optimization as SparseGPT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Wanda ranks N:M entries using weight magnitude times activation statistics, without Hessian inversion or error compensation. Sparsity does not make them equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both can keep half the weights but retain different entries and handle error differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0aab02eef15816d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5cba78153fef71c9">Why verify bit counts and value order in 32-column sparse packs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At 50% sparsity each group must contain 16 set bits and values packed in increasing retained-column order. Mismatches read wrong weights. Dense zero-multiplication is not sparse SpMV.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Packed value two maps to the second set bit, not original column two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5cba78153fef71c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-transformer" data-paper-title="Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-switch-transformer-9afbb109" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3ee5dc08bd3f4dc">How does Switch increase parameters without using all experts per token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-transformer">Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Brain</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
